The vast majority of Americans big-game hunting in Africa aren't cases of poaching, though it sounds like this dentist hired shady guides and either failed to secure the blessing of the wildlife management folks or was lied to about it having been secured.

In the wild, herding animals and territorial cats often have old males who, due to failing eyesight or other malady, start to terrorize their own herd. Old male rhinos and lions, for example, can kill breeding females or less-dominant males, and for animals facing extinction this kind of behavior simply can't be tolerated. In these cases Wildlife Rangers make the difficult decision to cull the male, and to generate funds for their conservation efforts take bids from big game hunters to do the deed and pay a premium for it. Instead of the violent males being killed by a random Ranger out of necessity, that same animal is then killed by a sport hunter who pays the salaries and upkeep for a dozen anti-poaching agents. This happens far more often than people realize, because old males are simply a fact of nature that must be managed.

While I'm 100% in support of getting to the bottom of the killing of this lion, which appears to have been done potentially in good faith but with bad guides, it's important to realize that rich fucks going to Africa to bag a big animal isn't always a bad thing. In fact, it's more often than not a very, very good thing.
